We welcome you to the Youth Commission meeting.

If you wish to address the Commission during the meeting, please complete a speaker’s card and give it
to the secretary. The maximum time for addressing the Commission is five minutes. If you wish to
address the Commission on an item which appears on the agenda, your comments will be heard during
the Commission’s discussion of that item. If you wish to address the Commission on a subject which
does not appear on the agenda but related to recreation or community service, you may make your
presentation under agenda item VII. Please be advised that the Commission cannot, under the State of
California’s Ralph M. Brown Act, take action on any item that does not appear on the agenda.

When making your presentation, please give your name and address for the record. Please make your
statement as brief as possible. Thank you.

Minutes
  Alhambra Youth Commission
  August 12, 2025

The Alhambra Youth Commission was called to order at 6:03 PM on August 12, 2025 at the Alhambra Civic Center
Library, 101 South 1st Street, Alhambra, CA 91801.

Call to Order
The meeting was called to order at 6:03 PM by Supervisor Rosalyn Rojas

Roll Call
Present: Deputy Director – Brie Houghton, Supervisor – Rosalyn Rojas, Vice President - Arabella Hernandez, Isabella
Hernandez, Natalia Rosales, Leslie Chu, Brendon Wu, Siqi Li, and Katherine Quintana
Absent: Pamela Ghazale, Chen Yu Wang, Lydia Chen

Flag Salute
The Pledge of Allegiance was recited with all members standing and participating.

Approval of Minutes (May 13, 2025 Meeting)
Motion to approve the minutes was made by Natalia Rosales and seconded by Brendon Wu. Motion passed by roll call
vote.

Staff Report
Supervisor Rojas introduced herself and noted absence from the previous meeting.
Recapped prior discussion topics:
   Spark of Love project.
   Possible involvement of President Pamela Ghazale with Councilmember Adele Andrade‐Stadler. This will be
  revisited at the next meeting. Requested updates or new project ideas from commissioners:
   Hello Neighbor ‐ suggested by Katherine Quintana; a Community gathering concept from Pasadena, suggested
  for possible implementation in Alhambra.
   Back to School Support ‐ suggested by Natalia Rosales; includes tutoring and/or fundraising for school supplies.
   Career Oriented Workshops ‐ suggested by Siqi Li; focused on high school students, possibly after school or on
  weekends, with a citywide reach.

Oral Communications
Marlene Buenrostro of Active San Gabriel Valley
Topic: Community Engagement with the Burke Heritage Stormwater Capture Project

Overview:

    Location: Behind the Alhambra Historical Society Museum.
    Purpose: Enhance park aesthetics, add recreational amenities, and install underground stormwater capture
  systems.
    Planned Features:
  o Native plants and trees.
  o Natural‐style playground.
  o Walkway and picnic areas.
  o Seasonal bioswale wetlands and biofiltration areas.
  o Educational signage about stormwater systems.
     Funding Sources:
  Safe Clean Water Program (LA County Flood Control District), Statewide Park Program Grant, CA Native
  Demonstration & Education Grant, City of Alhambra.
    Timeline: Construction anticipated February 2026; estimated duration of 15 months.

Commission Feedback:

    Likes: Open green space, flat terrain for sports, quiet and less crowded atmosphere.
    Challenges: Small size, low visibility, lack of amenities, limited parking.
    Opportunities: Increase awareness, add inviting features, target multiple age groups, and encourage
  environmental education.
    Concerns: Hidden location, limited community awareness, parking challenges.
    Support for Project: General support expressed; seen as beneficial for recreation, community engagement,
  environmental education, and stormwater management.
    Most Anticipated Outcomes: Educational signage, natural play features, improved usability, and increased
  community presence.

Commissioner Orals
Suki Li requests for earlier notice (2–3 weeks) before community engagement events to improve attendance. Supervisor
Rojas suggested creating a list of upcoming city events for commissioners to review and identify interest areas.
Discussion on commission priorities: event planning versus facilitation, with consensus to clarify roles and improve
internal communication.
Concern noted regarding attendance; importance of commissioner commitment emphasized.

Adjournment
Commissioner Brendon Wu calls the meeting to adjourn at 6:00 PM. Seconded by Arabella Hernandez
